title: Elements, compounds and mixtures sorted
examples: What is the difference between an element and a compound?
Is air a compound or a mixture?
What is a mixture in chemistry?

explain.say: Look around your kitchen: salt, water, the air you breathe. Chemists sort every material into just three boxes. Look at the board. Can you guess why gold sits in a different box from water?

See the first box? An element is made of only one kind of atom. An atom is the tiniest bit of a substance. Gold is only gold atoms, oxygen only oxygen atoms. There are 118 elements in all. Can you name one more?

Now the second box. A compound is two or more elements joined by chemical bonds. Water is hydrogen and oxygen held tight together. Salt is sodium and chlorine. It is a brand new substance. Are you surprised that salt comes from a soft metal and a poisonous gas?

Look at the third box. In a mixture, things are only mingled, not joined. Air is nitrogen, oxygen and other gases moving about together. You can separate a mixture quite easily, like picking peas out of rice. Which box would muddy water go in?

Great job! Now you can see the big difference side by side. A compound has a fixed recipe and new properties; a mixture can be any amounts, and each part stays itself. Challenge: stir iron and sulfur powder and it is a mixture. Heat it, and it becomes a compound!

faq.a: An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom. Chemical reactions cannot split it into anything simpler. Gold, oxygen and carbon are elements.
A compound is two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. Water, H2O, always has two hydrogen atoms for every oxygen atom.
A mixture is two or more substances mingled together but not chemically joined. Each part keeps its own properties, and you can separate them by physical methods like filtering.
asks: Is air a compound or a mixture?

faq.q: What is the difference between a compound and a mixture?
faq.a: In a compound the elements are chemically joined in a fixed ratio and have new properties. In a mixture the parts are just mingled, in any amounts, and keep their own properties.
There are 118 known elements. About 90 are found naturally on Earth; the rest have been made in laboratories.
asks: How many elements are on the periodic table?

facts: Air is a mixture, mostly nitrogen (about 78 percent) and oxygen (about 21 percent).

quiz.say: Which of these is a compound?
quiz.show: Which of these is a compound?
quiz.why: Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined in a fixed ratio.

wrong.0: Air is a mixture of gases that are not joined together.
wrong.2: Oxygen is an element: only oxygen atoms.

quiz.say: Iron filings and sulfur powder are stirred together but not heated. What do you have?
quiz.show: Iron filings and sulfur powder are stirred together but not heated. What do you have?
quiz.why: They are only mingled; a magnet can still pull the iron out.

wrong.1: A compound only forms when they react, for example when heated.
wrong.2: Stirring can never make a new element.
